description: Team OrbitalSAR Reflex (Volkan Dagli, Murat Emre ÖZKAYA, Prenses Metin) builds an open-source multi-sensor SAR observatory uniting NASA NISAR L2 GCOV/GUNW, ASF UAVSAR, Sentinel-1 RTC, and Meteomatics weather intelligence across 4 verified global regions (Göksu Delta, Hayward Fault, Amazon, Malaspina Glacier), distilling alerts into CRC-16 24-byte packets. Live app: https://orbitalsar.space/
summary: OrbitalSAR Reflex is an open-source multi-sensor radar observatory that translates NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) L-band observations, Sentinel-1 C-band imagery, and Meteomatics high-resolution weather data into intuitive surface-change intelligence. While radar sees through clouds and darkness, gigabyte-scale SAR products delay rapid interpretation during floods, fault creep, wildfires, and glacial surges. Our platform combines interactive orbital swath mapping, a real NASA NISAR GCOV/GUNW polarization and interferogram wipe comparator, and synced precipitation timelines across four study regions—anchored by our hometown Göksu Delta and Mersin-Taurus watershed (where Meteomatics recorded a 42.59 mm storm pulse alongside a -6.02 dB SAR backscatter drop). Finally, an edge-ready 24-byte CRC-16 binary reflex encoder (24B little-endian frame + CRC-16) compresses critical anomaly alerts by >7.5x10^7x for narrowband disaster response, bit-identical in Python and browser JavaScript.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
OrbitalSAR Reflex bridges the gap between gigabyte-scale Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) granules and actionable public or emergency decisions by linking radar scattering physics (roughness, dielectric constant, interferometric coherence, and Radar Vegetation Index shifts) with real meteorological observations and ultra-compact edge telemetry.

1. Verified Multi-Source Data Pipeline (src/nasa_stac_client.py & src/build_verified_datasets.py):
- NASA Earthdata CMR NISAR L2 Provisional: Real L-band GCOV (C2854338529-ASF) covariance products and 12-day repeat-pass GUNW (C2854335566-ASF) unwrapped interferograms.
- NASA ASF Vertex: Sentinel-1 and Quad-Pol airborne UAVSAR L-band scenes.
- Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC: Live sentinel-1-rtc scene discovery and previews without account barriers.
- Meteomatics Weather API: Synced 24h precipitation, 2m temperature, wind speed, and relative humidity series aligned directly to SAR acquisition timestamps.

2. Live Interactive Web Observatory (https://orbitalsar.space/):
Explore four verified study regimes—Göksu Delta & Mersin-Taurus Basin, Turkey (FLOOD_INUNDATION, -6.02 dB drop synced with 42.59 mm Meteomatics storm peak), Hayward Fault & Sacramento Delta, California (SURFACE_DEFORMATION using NISAR GUNW + NASA UAVSAR), Central Amazon Floodplain (WILDFIRE_SCAR / L-band canopy penetration), and Malaspina Glacier, Alaska (GLACIER_SURGE gated at -3.8 C). Includes an interactive Leaflet swath map, draggable SAR layer wipe comparator (HHHH/HVHV/GUNW/S1-RTC), Meteomatics weather chart, and live browser CORS queries to NASA CMR & Planetary Computer.

3. 24-Byte Deterministic Edge Telemetry (24B LE frame: uint32 + 4x float32 + 2x uint8 + CRC-16):
Distills critical disaster triggers from ~1.8 GB SAR granules into exact 24-byte binary packets (>7.5x10^7x alert compression) with byte-identical encoders in Python (src/sar_reflex_core.py) and browser JavaScript (assets/app.js), plus one-click .bin packet export.

Tools, Code & Verification:
Python 3 (zero external dependencies), HTML5/CSS3/Vanilla JS, Leaflet.js, and 11/11 passing automated unit tests (tests/test_sar_reflex_core.py, tests/test_nasa_stac_client.py). Mission patch imagery includes a visible "SI-GENERATED" corner watermark with zero NASA logos/emblems; code and documentation scaffolding were also AI/SI-assisted and independently verified via 11/11 automated unit tests.
